title: Integrating graph learning and meta-learning to enhance PET hydrolase activity at elevated temperatures
abstract: The identification and design of efficient biocatalysts to address plastic waste accumulation are pressing global challenges. Leveraging recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), we developed an integrated machine-learning framework incorporating the geometric vector perceptron-graph neural network and learn2learn models to yield robust and thermostable variants based on three representative polyethylene terephthalate hydrolases (i.e., FAST-PETase, DepoPETase, and BHETase). The engineered hydrolase variants demonstrated up to a 5.5-fold improvement in hydrolytic activity across a temperature range of 40°C–70°C compared to the wild-type enzymes. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed key microenvironmental interactions sustaining hydrolytic activity at high temperatures—enhanced hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions around active sites—and highlighted the unbound dynamics of bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate and mono-(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate near catalytic sites, motivating a two-enzyme system that achieved a 1.5-fold increase in terephthalic acid production. This study demonstrates a scalable AI-guided strategy for evolving robust polyethylene terephthalate hydrolases for industrial biodegradation. • Two-round machine learning discovers thermostable PET hydrolase variants • Meta-learning improves mutation compatibility and catalytic efficiency • MD-driven two-enzyme system achieves 1.5-fold increase in TPA yield Li et al. present a two-round machine-learning framework integrating GVP-GNN and meta-learning to evolve robust PET hydrolases. The engineered variants exhibit enhanced thermostability and catalytic efficiency, while a two-enzyme system achieves a 1.5-fold increase in terephthalic acid production from PET.

title: Hierarchical optimization of perovskite solar cell fabrication via step-by-step machine learning
abstract: Scalable manufacturing of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains challenging due to the need for efficient co-optimization of multiple interdependent process parameters across stepwise fabrication stages. Here, we propose a machine-learning-driven multi-target Bayesian optimization (MTBO) framework that integrates adaptive constraints with hierarchical objective optimization to guide full process optimization. Applied to electrospray deposition, MTBO simultaneously optimized six processing parameters and five target variables related to perovskite absorbers. By incorporating the characterization results of precursor solubility, perovskite crystallinity, and film quality as adaptive constraints, MTBO ensures that optimization stays within feasible manufacturing conditions while hierarchically prioritizing optimization targets of carrier lifetime and film homogeneity aligned with fabrication workflow. Under MTBO-optimized conditions, a champion PSC based on a 1.63 eV FA 0.82 Cs 0.18 Pb(I 0.86 Br 0.11 Cl 0.03 ) 3 perovskite achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.95%. These results demonstrate that MTBO enables autonomous and intelligent optimization across a multi-stage, multi-target fabrication workflow, paving the way toward self-driving laboratories for scalable PSC manufacturing.

title: AutoLoop is an autoregressive deep learning method for protein loop prediction with high accuracy
abstract: Protein structure prediction remains a key challenge in biology, with loop regions being essential for protein function yet difficult to model accurately. Herein, we propose AutoLoop, a computational model designed to automatically generate accurate loop backbone conformations. Uniquely, AutoLoop employs a bidirectional training approach while merging atom- and residue-level embedding, thus bolstering its robustness and precision. To validate its efficacy, we compare AutoLoop with thirteen established methods, including FREAD, NGK, AlphaFold2, and AlphaFold3. The results indicate that AutoLoop consistently outperforms other methods, achieving a median root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of 1.12 Å on the CASP15 dataset, also maintaining its superior performance on the HOMSTARD dataset. The addition of a post-processing module enhances AutoLoop's performance slightly, reflecting the sound reliability of the predicted backbone structures. Additionally, the case study demonstrates AutoLoop's ability to capture one or several dominant loop conformations. These advancements hold great promise for protein engineering and drug discovery.

title: Embedded bioprinting with multiscale on-demand sub-voxel assembly for integrated coordination
abstract: Extrusion-based bioprinting struggles to replicate the cross-scale heterogeneity of native tissues, where micron-scale features must integrate seamlessly within centimeter-scale architectures. We present multiscale on-demand sub-voxel assembly for integrated coordination (MOSAIC), an embedded bioprinting framework that enables dynamic programming of internal filament patterns, referred to as sub-voxels, synchronized with global geometry during continuous printing. MOSAIC combines a physics-informed model of multi-material filament formation and hierarchical path planning to achieve controlled heterogeneity from approximately 0.03 cm micro-patterns to 2 cm structures in a single uninterrupted process. We demonstrate this capability through anatomically inspired constructs: a dual-layer artery model integrating soft-to-stiff gradients for physiological compliance and an intestinal model combining micro-scale villi and millimeter-scale folds with spatially organized cells. This approach expands the design space of embedded bioprinting, overcoming static material constraints and enabling efficient fabrication of multiscale architectures that are critical for advanced tissue models.

title: Chemical language models for generating compounds with triple-target activity
abstract: Polypharmacology-based drug discovery relies on compounds with multi-target activity that are identified in screening and target profiling assays or using computational methods. Contemporary design of multi-target compounds is advanced by deep generative modeling. Dual-target compounds (DT-CPDs) are known for having a large number of target combinations, providing a sound basis for machine learning. By contrast, only comparably small numbers of triple-target compounds (TT-CPDs) are available, covering a very limited target space. Here, we investigate how this data restriction might be overcome to enable generative design of new TT-CPDs. Therefore, a transformer model is pre-trained to generate DT-CPDs from corresponding single-target compounds and used as a base model for triple-target fine-tuning. For different target combinations, the resulting models correctly reproduce known TT-CPDs not encountered during fine-tuning. Feature importance analysis explains the predictions and reveals structural motifs implicated in target selectivity or triple-target activity, thus providing a chemically intuitive rationale for the approach.

title: Convolutional neural networks and volcano plots for screening and predicting two-dimensional single-atom catalysts in CO2 reduction
abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) emerge as pivotal frontiers for catalyzing diverse reactions, but identifying optimal combinations of active elements, supports, and coordination environments eludes traditional methods. This study integrates multi-branch convolutional neural network (CNN) models with hybrid descriptor-based activity volcano plots to screen 2D SACs for efficient CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR). Since single electronic descriptors, such as the d -band center, are insufficient to predict catalytic activity, our CNN model uses 2D electronic density of states (eDOS) to predict adsorption energies. Hybrid descriptors combining both C- and O-type CO 2 RR intermediates are used to construct volcano plots and limit potential maps for screening catalysts capable of efficient CO 2 RR. To explore the electronic scale principle governing practical CO 2 RR activity, orbital-wise eDOS occlusion and shifting analysis based on the CNN model are employed to examine the adsorption energy and, consequently, catalytic activities while varying supported single atoms, which offers a tangible framework to design efficient SACs.

title: A unifying geometric framework for computational representation of stereoisomers based on mixed product
abstract: Analyzing molecular chirality, encompassing the determination of stereoisomers' configurations and quantification of the degree of chirality, is critical for drug discovery. However, current methods struggle with complex chirality and lack quantification capabilities. We propose a unifying geometric solution based on mixed product representation for chirality quantification. This approach unifies chiral stereoisomer discrimination by directly mapping molecular symmetry breaking to a 3D algebraic space. Unlike conventional qualitative rules such as the Cahn-Ingold-Prelog rules, this method provides quantitative descriptors for each stereogenic element. We implement this approach in ChiralFinder, a computational tool that achieves high accuracy in differentiating conformations and automates the analysis of central and axial chirality. The benchmarking results demonstrate that ChiralFinder effectively detects and distinguishes stereogenic elements and integrates with machine learning models to enhance spectra prediction. This rigorous geometric framework establishes a foundation for comprehensive stereoisomer representation, with potential for expansion to include planar and helical chirality.

title: Searching for high-performance thermoelectric materials via an advanced machine learning framework
abstract: Data quality, feature engineering, and model generalization are key challenges in applying machine learning to high-performance materials design. Here, we report a framework addressing these challenges using thermoelectric materials as a case study. Data are collected and curated from the Starrydata2 database, followed by multi-step feature engineering, including construction, selection, and optimization, to obtain a physically meaningful subset. By benchmarking against mainstream regression models, with independent external dataset testing and model interpretability analysis, a modified tabular prior-data fitted network (TabPFN) model (model I) demonstrates superior accuracy and generalization in predicting the thermoelectric figure of merit ( ZT ). Model I is applied to halide double perovskites from the Materials Project database, identifying candidates including Rb 2 CuSbCl 6 , Cs 2 AgAuCl 6 , and Rb 2 CuBiCl 6 . First-principles calculations validate their thermoelectric properties, with n-type Cs 2 AgAuCl 6 achieving ZT max = 1.64 at 800 K. These results highlight the potential of a data-driven and computationally synergistic approach for discovering high-performance thermoelectric materials.

title: Computational approaches for RNA structure prediction and design
abstract: Determining the three-dimensional (3D) structure of RNA is crucial for understanding its diverse biological functions. The field of computational RNA structure prediction has recently been transformed by deep learning, which has dramatically improved accuracy beyond that of conventional homology- and de novo modeling approaches. This article overviews these advancements. We first summarize the principles of foundational conventional approaches before detailing the current state-of-the-art deep-learning-based approaches. Deep-learning-based approaches are categorized into strategies that leverage multiple sequence alignments (MSAs), recent MSA-free methods that rely on single sequences, and emerging generalist models that can predict entire heterogenic biomolecular complexes. Furthermore, we discuss how these predictive breakthroughs are accelerating the field of RNA design. Finally, we outline the current challenges and future directions for computational RNA structural biology.

title: Physics-informed full-field strain reconstruction in large-format lithium-ion batteries using distributed optical fiber sensing
abstract: Mechanical strain monitoring in lithium-ion batteries is essential for ensuring structural integrity and operational safety. Conventional point-based measurements, however, lack sufficient spatial resolution to capture complex deformation patterns, especially in large-format batteries. Here, we report a distributed optical fiber sensor deployed on an 81.4 Ah large-format pouch battery to provide continuous spatial strain monitoring. The resulting one-dimensional strain data are first mapped onto the two-dimensional surface via a feature-point projection method. A physics-informed reconstruction algorithm then generates the full-field strain distribution. The reconstructed strain fields exhibit mean absolute errors of 12.278, 17.759, and 22.728 με for 0.5C, 1C, and 1.5C, respectively, confirming the accuracy and reliability of the proposed method. Furthermore, thermal and intercalation-induced strains are quantitatively decoupled, which reveals the characteristic evolution patterns under various C-rates and cycling stages. This sensing-mapping-reconstruction framework provides valuable spatially distributed data for battery state evaluation and early fault diagnosis.

title: Artificial intelligence for NMR chemical shift prediction
abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a key technique for the determination of molecular structure, but accurate chemical shift prediction remains challenging due to data limitations and the high computational cost of quantum mechanical methods, such as density functional theory (DFT) and gauge-including atomic orbital (GIAO). Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) provide fast and scalable alternatives with near DFT accuracy. The field has evolved from descriptor-based models and neural networks (NNs) toward deep learning (DL) approaches, particularly graph neural networks (GNNs) and transformers, which learn molecular representations directly from 2D and three-dimensional (3D) structures. These models have been applied to multiple nuclei and complex molecular systems, with hybrid quantum mechanics (QM)-ML and solvent-aware methods improving accuracy and realism. Despite progress, challenges remain in data quality, generalization to new chemical spaces, and uncertainty quantification. This review summarizes recent methods, datasets, benchmarking practices, and broader AI applications in NMR analysis and spectral processing.

title: Inverse design of metamaterials with manufacturing-guiding spectrum-to-structure conditional diffusion model
abstract: Metamaterials are artificially engineered structures that manipulate electromagnetic waves, exhibiting optical properties absent in natural materials. Recently, machine learning for the inverse design of metamaterials has drawn attention. However, the highly nonlinear relationship between metamaterial structures and optical behavior, coupled with fabrication difficulties, poses challenges for using machine learning to design and manufacture complex metamaterials. Herein, we propose a general framework that implements customized spectrum-to-shape and size parameters to address one-to-many metamaterial inverse design problems using conditional diffusion models. Our method exhibits superior spectral prediction accuracy, generates a diverse range of patterns compared to other typical generative models, and offers valuable prior knowledge for manufacturing through subsequent analysis of the diverse generated results, thereby facilitating the experimental fabrication of metamaterial designs. We demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method by successfully designing and fabricating a free-form metamaterial with a tailored selective emission spectrum for thermal camouflage applications.

title: Axiomatic decoupling to surpass constraints in large-scale brain-like emulation
abstract: Conventional neuromorphic chips face challenges in achieving large-scale emulation due to limitations in neuron and synapse density and restricted emulation capabilities. This work presents an innovative axiomatic decoupling method designed specifically for high-density neuromorphic emulation. The resulting axiomatic-decoupled neuromorphic architecture (ADNA) combines the dense computational power of application-specific integrated circuits , the flexibility of general-purpose chips, and the vast memory capacity of modern storage technologies to overcome traditional constraints in neuromorphic emulator development. A key advancement in ADNA is its neuromorphic computing chip, which significantly surpasses existing standards for neuron and synapse densities. This architecture incorporates general-purpose chip-based emulation logic, enabling real-time access to computing data via a state-aware channel, thereby substantially improving neuromorphic emulation capabilities. ADNA also facilitates large-scale storage of neural network parameters using dedicated memory devices while maintaining scalability. Furthermore, multimodal signal-based neuromorphic emulation is demonstrated on a dual-chip platform.

title: Large language model-based fault diagnosis for lithium-ion batteries in cloud-edge systems
abstract: Recurring safety incidents involving lithium-ion batteries raise concerns about reliability and call for robust fault diagnosis, especially when edge-based methods struggle under complex conditions. Here we report a cloud-edge framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) for battery fault diagnosis. We introduce a down-sampling method based on data disorder degree (DDP) to compress signals, and we develop a hierarchical, fine-tuned LLM architecture that sequentially performs fault detection, fault-type identification, and severity grading. We evaluate the framework on more than 3,000 samples from five battery types, combining laboratory measurements with real-world energy-storage data. Across model scales, we identify a 7-billion-parameter model with 4-bit quantization as the best trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. This configuration classifies and grades faults with accuracies of 99.2% and 96.8%, respectively, and it significantly outperforms conventional methods.

title: Detecting electrolyte wetting defects in lithium-ion batteries based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
abstract: Electrolyte wetting defects generated during the wetting process compromise the safety and consistency of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), making reliable detection at the manufacturing stage essential. Here, we report a data-driven detection method for wetting defects based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). We perform EIS measurements on pouch cells after injection but before formation, using ultrasonic C-scan results as non-destructive labels. Analysis of a 100-cell dataset identifies physics-informed EIS response features, including high-frequency ohmic resistance shifts, and mid-frequency charge-transfer perturbations. A few-shot learning algorithm with an asymmetric prototypical network classifies these defects. Cross-validation demonstrates that this method achieves a detection accuracy of 98.0% ± 2.0% under minute-scale measurements, confirming feasibility under limited data conditions. Compared with imaging techniques, the EIS-driven approach offers superior throughput and lower cost. This method provides a practical pathway for online full inspection in large-scale manufacturing, enhancing yield, lifetime, and safety.

title: General trend of strain effect on the adsorption and reactions over metal surfaces
abstract: Strain effect can effectively regulate catalytic performance, as tensile (compressive) strain shifts the d-band center of metal surfaces, strengthening (weakening) adsorption energies. While this rationale can explain strain effects qualitatively, a general quantitative description across different metals is lacking. Here, we report that a dual-descriptor scaling relation can describe the response of adsorption energy and activation energy to lattice strain on close-packed metal surfaces. By classifying adsorbates according to their electronegativity, we show that a general adsorbate exhibits the combined features of strong- and weak-electronegativity adsorbates. The dual-descriptor model can account for these features and reliably predict both stationary- and transition-state energetics. We further clarify the physical origin of the distinct responses of different adsorbates using machine learning classification. This study advances the understanding of strain effects in heterogeneous catalysis and provides a quantitative framework for rational catalyst design.

title: Digital twins of the earth can take energy systems modeling to the next level
abstract: Digital twins of the Earth are an emerging field of research and development. Institutions like the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration have started ambitious initiatives to develop highly accurate digital replicas of the Earth system. These initiatives not only push the frontiers in global climate and weather modeling by making massive use of the largest supercomputers and AI but also set new standards in co-design and user engagement, allowing users to express needs and requirements right from the beginning of the developments. For the energy sector, Earth system digital twins bear great potential to overcome some of the major challenges in climate-energy modeling. In this perspective, we describe paths forward to bring the climate science and energy systems modeling communities closer together by leveraging the vast capabilities of Earth system digital twins, and we identify gaps, requirements, and recommendations for further developments.

title: Quotient-complex transformer for perovskite data analysis
abstract: The identification of advanced functional materials is critical for addressing challenges in sustainable energy and climate change. Hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites (HOIPs) have attracted significant interest due to their exceptional optoelectronic properties for photovoltaics. While geometric deep learning, particularly graph neural networks (GNNs), has shown promise for material property prediction, conventional GNNs struggle to capture periodicity and higher-order interactions inherent in crystalline materials. To overcome these limitations, we propose a quotient (cellular) complex (QC)-based structural representation and introduce the quotient-complex transformer (QCformer). By modeling materials as QCs, our approach naturally incorporates periodicity and many-body interactions through simplices of varying dimensions. Experiments on HOIP band-gap prediction demonstrate that QCformer outperforms state-of-the-art models, highlighting its effectiveness for perovskite materials.

title: Early calendar life and health prediction of silicon batteries via machine learning with uncertainty quantification
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries with silicon anodes promise high energy density but are limited by calendar lifetime. Reducing the long iteration time to obtain experimental results requires predicting calendar lifetime early in a cell's life. In this study, we demonstrate that lightweight machine learning models with feature engineering can provide calendar lifetime estimates from early electrochemical signals. After 1 month of electrochemical aging, the best models achieve 10% error in calendar-life prediction and can separate "bad" from "good" lifetime cells with a mean F1 score of 0.857. As battery systems exhibit inherent variability, four methods for uncertainty quantification are compared, and confidence intervals are demonstrated with an uncertainty of ±3.6 months in lifetime prediction. A feature importance analysis indicates that early patterns in voltage decay are the strongest indicators of calendar lifetime. Finally, this modeling approach has high error when generalizing to new electrode chemistries or testing conditions but with appropriately low confidence.

title: Artificial intelligence shaping the future of hydrogen technologies
abstract: Hydrogen energy is considered pivotal for achieving a carbon-neutral future, yet it faces significant challenges in terms of cost-effective production, efficient storage, and scalable catalyst development. Traditional experimental and computational approaches are often slow and resource-intensive. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) is rapidly transforming the hydrogen technology landscape by enabling accelerated discovery and optimization processes. This review comprehensively discusses the recent advances in AI for catalyst discovery in hydrogen evolution and oxygen evolution reactions and its role in optimizing hydrogen production systems, such as electrolysis, photocatalysis, and thermochemical water splitting. Additionally, it covers machine-learning-driven insights into hydrogen storage materials, including metal hydrides, metal-organic frameworks, and liquid organic hydrogen carriers. The key challenges, data strategies, and emerging techniques such as explainable AI, generative models, and digital twins are also addressed. The review concludes with future directions and perspectives on how AI and ML can revolutionize the hydrogen economy.

title: Explaining a molecular diffusion model
abstract: Diffusion models have gained considerable importance in many scientific fields. These models perturb the original data distributions by adding noise during the diffusion phase, which is then removed again during the subsequent denoising phase when generating the output. Predictions of diffusion are difficult to rationalize. Current efforts to explain the generative process and outputs of diffusion models are essentially limited to training data attribution for image generation. Herein, we report a feature attribution approach to better understand how diffusion models used in molecular design arrive at their results. As a proof of concept, we analyze an equivariant diffusion model for generating linkers in fragment-based compound design. The analysis yields plausible explanations for linker predictions and uncovers unexpected atomic contributions to generative design. Notably, the equivariant diffusion model does not require learning the underlying chemistry to produce chemically sound compound structures.

title: Colorimetric biosensors for pathogen detection toward accessible and scalable diagnostics
abstract: Colorimetric biosensors are emerging as versatile analytical platforms for healthcare, environmental monitoring, and food safety by converting biological interactions into visible signals for rapid, cost-effective detection. Advances in nanobiotechnology and materials science, including inorganic nanoparticles, metal-organic frameworks, and quantum dots, have enhanced sensitivity through signal amplification and tunable optical properties. Integration with microfluidics, smartphone-based imaging, machine learning, and Internet of Things platforms has enabled portable, real-time diagnostics. Emerging wearable and multiplexed formats further expand accessibility and sustainability. However, challenges remain in ensuring stability, selectivity in complex matrices, reproducibility, and large-scale manufacturing for widespread deployment. This perspective highlights emerging directions in nanobiotechnology-driven colorimetric biosensors, exemplified by coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) detection platforms developed during the global severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) pandemic. Rather than cataloging sensing chemistries alone, this perspective advances a translational roadmap that connects physical sensing principles, nanobiotechnology advances, and digital integration strategies to enable scalable, field-deployable diagnostic platforms.

title: Developing ChemMLLM as a multimodal large language model for chemistry
abstract: Recent years have seen rapid progress in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in the field of chemistry. However, chemical MLLMs capable of handling cross-modal understanding and generation remain underexplored. To fill this gap, we propose ChemMLLM, a unified chemical MLLM for molecule understanding and generation. In this work, we design five types of multimodal tasks across text, molecular simplified molecular input line entry system (SMILES) strings, and images and curate the datasets. We benchmark ChemMLLM against a range of general leading MLLMs, chemical LLMs, and specialized models on these tasks. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of a unified multimodal interface. Our work extends the capabilities of chemical MLLMs to the realm of image generation, demonstrating the feasibility of unifying multiple cross-modal chemical tasks within a single mode l and enabling more intuitive, visual human-artificial intelligence (AI) interaction.

title: Real-world VOC exposure and health implications in recreational vehicles under climate stress
abstract: Rising mobile living and frequent extreme climate events make recreational vehicles (RVs) a critical microenvironment with notable exposure risks. Here, we conduct field observations in an RV under sealed conditions by measuring the concentrations of 22 typical volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and examining the influence of environmental parameters on VOC dynamics and exposure risks. Results reveal long-tail characteristics of VOCs, dominated by formaldehyde (average concentration of 118.9 μg/m 3 ), that exceed the WHO guideline limit. Material surface temperature and external heat load are identified as key influencing factors of VOC dynamics. An interpretable deep learning model is developed to extract influencing factors and predict VOC change patterns. Risk assessment indicates that the potential risks from formaldehyde exposure in RVs are high among those of the reported vehicle types. By establishing an integrated framework incorporating real-world measurements, predictive modeling, and risk assessment, this study provides a basis for understanding VOC dynamics in mobile living environments.

title: AI-driven next-gen health monitoring via flexible sensors to decode breath
abstract: Respiratory dynamic patterns offer a unique window into the body's cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and neurological functions, yet continuous and accurate capture of such signals is fundamentally challenged by the mismatch between sensing interfaces and dynamic biological tissues. This review focuses on the convergence of flexible material innovations and artificial intelligence (AI) analytics to outline the development of next-generation intelligent respiratory monitoring. It systematically examines bioinspired flexible strain and humidity sensors with microstructural designs, elaborating on their medical-grade accuracy in quantifying respiratory parameters and the central role of material-device co-design in boosting sensing performance, comfort, and robustness. AI's function as a powerful signal decoder, enabling at-home lung function measurement, anomaly detection, and cross-disciplinary digital biomarker extraction for disease screening, is discussed. The review constructs a material-to-integration-to-intelligent interpretation technological paradigm advancing personalized medicine, envisions its value in chronic disease management and remote monitoring, and identifies key clinical translation challenges to provide forward-looking research perspectives.

Predicting battery performance with small datasets by enhancing machine learning with distribution of relaxation times analysis
abstract: Accurate battery diagnostic models often struggle in capturing complex degradation mechanisms. Here, we report a combined approach using distribution of relaxation time (DRT) analysis and machine learning (ML) of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data to diagnose and predict the performance of solid-state batteries. The dataset has 112 impedance measurements collected over 100 cycles from eight TDK CeraCharge batteries. Using EIS features and the applied charge-discharge rate, the models estimate battery capacity at a given cycle and predict the capacity after the subsequent ten cycles. ML methods, including Bayesian regression, Gaussian process regression, neural networks, and decision trees, achieve accurate diagnostics (mean absolute error 1.6%) and prediction (2.4%). DRT-based feature selection identifies the most informative frequency range (15 Hz–1.5 kHz) and improves training efficiency. Tomography reveals mechanical degradation, i.e., volume expansion and fractures, which increases impedance and contributes to capacity loss. This approach enables accurate, data-driven battery diagnostics and forecasting.

title: A universal deep learning framework for digital PCR and ELISA
abstract: Image-processing frameworks are critical for the absolute quantification of nucleic acids and proteins, in which accurate analysis of microreactors generated by digital PCR or digital ELISA is required. However, existing methods often suffer from reduced accuracy at high microreactor densities and limited generalizability. Here, we propose Microreactor-Vision, a deep learning framework that integrates an enhanced U-Net-based segmentation model with a lightweight convolutional neural network classifier. The framework achieves >99% quantitative accuracy and has been validated across multiple fluorescence channels and diverse microreactor architectures. Microreactor-Vision further demonstrates an ultra-low limit of detection and a broad dynamic range (10 −1 –10 4 copies/μL), with strong linearity between predicted and actual concentrations (coefficient of determination [R 2 ] > 0.99). To our knowledge, it achieves the highest detection throughput and accuracy reported to date while maintaining efficient inference speed. Microreactor-Vision offers a rapid, cost-effective, and robust solution for AI-driven absolute quantification, supporting translational and clinical biosensing applications.

title: A multi-agent AI framework for explainable battery system maintenance
abstract: The operation and maintenance (O&M) of battery energy-storage systems (BESSs) remain dominated by reactive, expert-dependent diagnostics. Although cell-level inconsistencies can provide early warning signals of degradation and safety risks, the lack of scalable and interpretable decision-support frameworks prevents these signals from being effectively translated into operational actions. Here, we introduce an inconsistency-driven O&M paradigm for large-scale BESSs that systematically transforms routine monitoring data into explainable and decision-oriented guidance via large language model-based semantic reasoning. Using 8 months of field data from an in-service BESS comprising 3,564 cells, we demonstrate how real-world O&M queries are converted into actionable maintenance insights, reducing response time and operational cost by over 80% compared with conventional expert-driven practices. These results establish a scalable pathway for intelligent O&M of BESSs, with direct implications for reliability and cost-effective integration of energy storage into modern power systems.

title: Data-driven molecular design rules for electrolytes in CO2 electroreduction
abstract: CO 2 electroreduction offers a promising route to convert CO 2 into valuable chemicals and fuels. CO 2 electroreduction research has predominantly focused on catalyst innovation, yet the electrolyte, equally critical for governing CO 2 solubility and ion transport, remains comparatively underexplored. Here, we introduce a multiscale informatics framework integrating density functional theory, conductor-like screening model for realistic solvents (COSMO-RS) thermodynamics, molecular dynamics (MD), and machine learning to accelerate electrolyte discovery. The framework focuses on bulk-phase electrolyte properties that govern solvent stability, CO 2 solubility, and transport, and thus electrolyte performance in CO 2 electroreduction. Hierarchical screening of 1.3 million organic molecules identified six high-performing candidates, validated through MD simulations, and benchmarked against twenty experimentally tested electrolytes. All data, descriptors, and pretrained models are consolidated in the open-access COSMIC (CO 2 solvent materials informatics collection) database. Our analysis reveals how molecular polarity, protic character, and electronic structure govern CO 2 solubility and viscosity, providing transferable molecular design rules for next-generation CO 2 electroreduction electrolytes.

title: Transforming urban energy systems with scalable non-invasive building thermal sensing
abstract: The urgent need for sustainable buildings has accelerated the development of non-invasive sensing methods to assess thermal parameters, such as thermal transmittance, temperature, and humidity. Unlike intrusive traditional approaches that lack scalability, non-invasive techniques, including infrared thermography and ground-penetrating radar, offer contactless diagnostics. However, their transition into robust sensing systems is hindered by environmental sensitivity, a lack of standardization, and limited capacity to capture large-scale indoor-outdoor interactions. This review systematically analyzes these barriers and presents emerging integrated solutions. Key advancements include unmanned aerial vehicle multimodal sensing that enables high-throughput data collection and physics-informed learning frameworks that enhance measurement accuracy and model interoperability. These approaches can transform these techniques from isolated diagnostic tools into scalable urban-level intelligence systems. This transformation fundamentally strengthens building energy modeling at the city scale, providing critical data support for decarbonization pathways and climate-resilient urban planning.

title: Scientific AI systems require domain-aware robustness validation
abstract: AI has become an essential tool in many areas of scientific discovery. However, its robustness, particularly in high-stakes scientific applications, remains insufficiently understood. While adversarial vulnerabilities have been widely studied in image recognition, their implications in scientific disciplines, where physical constraints and numerical stability are critical, have not been thoroughly explored. This work presents a systematic evaluation of AI model fragility across five scientific domains: climate modeling, quantum chemistry, fluid dynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and wireless communications. We demonstrate that small, structured perturbations can destabilize predictions in all of these domains, even in models that achieve high accuracy under normal conditions. Furthermore, the failure patterns vary across domains, suggesting that these vulnerabilities are domain specific. Our findings underscore the importance of assessing AI robustness in scientific contexts and offer preliminary insights into how to design more resilient and reliable AI systems for scientific applications.

title: Geometry-constrained prediction of catalytically competent kinase domains across the human kinome
abstract: Accurate structural modeling of kinases across functional states helps to understand signaling networks. However, most human kinases lack experimentally determined active-state structures, and existing computational methods often fail to predict catalytically competent conformations. Here, we present a geometry-constrained modeling framework based on AFEXplorer (AFEX) that enables robust prediction of active, ATP- and magnesium-bound states for 436 catalytic kinase domains across the human kinome. By explicitly enforcing biophysical criteria, AFEX overcomes the template dependence and conformational bias inherent in AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold3. Benchmarking against 156 kinase-substrate complexes shows that AFEX achieves a sub-2 Å backbone root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) in 99% of cases and accurately recapitulates critical catalytic features with precise ATP coordination. Notably, AFEX correctly predicted active conformations for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2), whereas AlphaFold3 failed. These improvements are consistent across kinase families, including both well-characterized kinases and those underrepresented in AlphaFold's training data. AFEX provides a generalizable framework for studying active conformations and dynamics in kinases.

title: Interpretable neural operators enable topology-optimized cooling for concentrating photovoltaics
abstract: Concentrating photovoltaic systems generate high electrical output but also severe heat loads that reduce efficiency and reliability. Here, we report an interpretable neural operator framework for designing topology-optimized cooling channels for concentrating photovoltaics. A deep operator network learns the mapping from variable-depth flow field geometries to temperature and pressure fields, enabling rapid design screening while reducing computational energy use by more than 99% compared with conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The optimized topology is fabricated by high-resolution stereolithography and tested under concentrated illumination. It lowers peak surface temperature from about 60°C to 54°C at 10 suns and is supported by numerical results showing a 15.7% increase in Nusselt number. Physical interpretation shows that topological undulations induce wall-normal secondary flows and improve field synergy, actively disrupting the thermal boundary layer. This framework provides a general route for interpretable, data-driven thermal fluid design in high-heat-flux energy devices.

title: Perovskite databases analysis using machine learning and large language models for prediction and reverse engineering
abstract: Perovskite solar cells have reached power conversion efficiencies exceeding 26.95% in single-junction devices and 34.85% in silicon/perovskite tandems, but stability remains a major barrier to commercialization. Here, we report machine learning and large language model (LLM)-based frameworks for analyzing open-access perovskite datasets to address both efficiency and stability challenges. Classical regression models and LLMs are combined to evaluate different data representations, embedding strategies, and hyperparameter configurations for predictive and inverse design tasks. LLMs are further employed to generate fabrication procedures targeting specific key performance indicators, while clustering analysis identifies trends associated with high efficiency and stability. The proposed approach produces optimized recommendations for stack materials, additives, and processing steps across complete perovskite solar cell fabrication, achieving predicted energy yields exceeding 4,000 kWh/m 2 . These results demonstrate the potential of LLM-assisted frameworks for accelerating the discovery and optimization of perovskite solar cells.

title: Explainable AI reveals the allosteric blind spot in protein-ligand binding predictions
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed prediction of protein structure and interactions, yet modeling of allosteric binding remains a persistent challenge. We develop an explainable AI framework that interrogates AI models AlphaFold3, Protenix, Boltz-2, Chai-1, and DynamicBind on rigorously stratified datasets of orthosteric and allosteric ligand-protein complexes. While AI models excel in accurate modeling of orthosteric ligand binding, a consistent and substantial performance gap observed across diverse architectures emerges in prediction of allosteric complexes. The biophysical logic for this dichotomy is unveiled through physics-based lens of the energy landscape theory. Orthosteric binding creates dominant energetic funnels via ligand-induced minimal frustration quenching, while allosteric sites preserve neutral frustration landscapes in both apo and holo protein states. By linking prediction outcomes to frustration landscapes, this study recasts AI shortcomings in prediction of allosteric ligand binding as diagnostic indicators of allostery, establishing a physics-informed framework that turns the allosteric blind spot into mechanistic insight.

title: Fusing generative AI and ML-FFs for inverse design and high-fidelity dynamic simulation of fused-ring aromatic hydrocarbons
abstract: Rational design of fused-ring aromatic hydrocarbons is hindered by vast chemical space, costly quantum simulations, and a disconnect between generation and dynamic validation. Here, we report an integrated computational platform that unifies physics-constrained generative AI, interpretable multi-objective screening, and high-fidelity machine-learning force fields (ML-FFs) to enable inverse design and dynamic simulation of fused-ring aromatic hydrocarbons. A physical consistency module incorporating the Brown-Ladner method and iterative molecular weight inversion enforces chemical and structural feasibility from the outset, generating diversity, novelty, and theoretically synthesizable structures validated against experimental benchmarks, while XGBoost predictors accurately forecast key electronic properties. We further developed DeepAsphalt-26, ML-FFs specifically optimized for aromatic systems, which attains density-functional-theory-level accuracy while accelerating molecular dynamics by two orders of magnitude, accurately reproducing π-π stacking dynamics and free energy landscapes. By bridging generative design and high-fidelity simulation, this workflow offers an end-to-end in silico route to engineering carbonaceous materials with targeted properties.

title: Large language models as designers for autonomous research of anisotropic polymer thermocells
abstract: Flexible thermoelectric materials face a persistent trade-off between output power and mechanical robustness. Here, we report OmniMat, a large language model-driven framework that designs experimental protocols in a human-in-the-loop workflow without relying on structured task-specific datasets. OmniMat integrates cross-disciplinary inspiration retrieval, mechanism-level screening, and expert-guided refinement to propose constant-velocity directional freezing in ethanol followed by salting-out reinforcement. This strategy creates continuous anisotropic ion channels within a strengthened poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) network. The representative 10 wt % medium-molecular-weight PVA (m-PVA) thermocell used for device validation delivers a normalized power density of 0.68 mW m − 2 K − 2 and toughness exceeding 21 MJ m − 3 . A flexible array maintains electrical output during stretching, bending, and partial cutting. These results establish a traceable route for language-model-assisted materials discovery in data-scarce research.

title: Molecular dynamics simulation and machine learning predict NMR shift distributions and dynamics in amorphous drug materials
abstract: Here, we report the use of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations plus machine-learned chemical shifts to predict the NMR spectra of amorphous forms of the drug materials irbesartan and valsartan. When using the C-rescale barostat, the linewidths of 13 C and 15 N spectra generated from shifts predicted by the ShiftML2 machine-learning model were in excellent agreement with the experiment, demonstrating that the effects of fast motions (" β relaxation") were correctly described. Measurements of 13 C shift anisotropies confirmed the results of MD simulation in which the glass transition has no impact on molecular reorientation, while 1 H T 1ρ measurements indicate that diffusional motion dominates the slower dynamics (" α relaxation"). Together, MD and NMR provide a comprehensive picture of structure and dynamics in these systems on either side of the glass transition.

title: Ultra-fast battery health estimation from random 100 mV charging fragments using conditional generative diffusion
abstract: State-of-health (SOH) estimation is essential for lithium-ion battery management. However, real-world disruptions often result in fragmented battery data, making reliable SOH estimation challenging. Generative artificial intelligence offers a promising paradigm to address these limitations. Here, we present a conditional diffusion framework that generates complete battery data from random charging fragments spanning 100 mV, including fragments as short as 20 mV, to estimate SOH. Validated on 89 batteries across three cathode chemistries and nine protocols, the framework delivers stable, high-fidelity generation that outperforms generative adversarial network (GAN) and variational autoencoder (VAE) baselines. It achieves SOH estimation errors as low as 0.18% mean absolute error (MAE) and demonstrates higher estimation accuracy and robustness than the evaluated baseline methods under diverse missing-data conditions. In most fast-charging scenarios, the framework requires only charging fragments shorter than 30 s to estimate SOH. These results demonstrate that conditional diffusion provides a practical solution for battery health estimation under data-limited conditions.

title: Intracranial delivery of neuron-preferential lipid nanoparticles for gene-editing activity in mouse brain
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are promising non-viral vectors for central nervous system (CNS) gene therapy, but effective delivery is limited by the blood-brain barrier and cell-type specificity. Here, we combined intracranial delivery with high-throughput, cluster-based screening and machine learning to identify LNP formulations optimized for functional neuronal gene-editing activity. We screened 720 LNP formulations for their ability to transfect neurons and deliver genetic payloads efficiently. Following this, cluster-mode intracranial screening enabled targeted delivery to specific brain regions, including the ventral posteromedial nucleus (VPM) and hippocampus, and efficiently narrowed hundreds of candidates to single optimized formulations. Optimized LNPs achieved approximately 20% gene editing, measured as functional activity, in targeted areas and exhibited neuron- and astrocyte-enriched transfection patterns. These results demonstrate that intracranial delivery, combined with machine-learning-guided optimization, can identify LNPs capable of precise cell- and region-preferential gene delivery, supporting the development of targeted therapies for neurological disorders.

title: Cryo-EM map and functional electron transport studies of the HoxEFU subcomplex of the HOX [NiFe]-hydrogenase from Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
abstract: The HOX [NiFe]-hydrogenase of Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 is composed of large (HoxH) and small (HoxY) subunits that catalyze H 2 activation and HoxE, HoxF, and HoxU subunits that catalyze reactions with NAD(H), ferredoxins, or flavodoxin. Here, we report single-particle cryoelectron microscopy (cryo-EM) and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy for kinetic modeling of electron transfer in the HoxEFU subcomplex. Cryo-EM of resting-state HoxEFU yielded a low-resolution map with space for a dimer of HoxEFU monomers. An AlphaFold model of the dimer identified inter-cofactor distances and was used with cofactor E m values determined here to calculate electron transfer rate constants, k ET , for individual steps. We used these values to model electron transfer kinetics for HoxEFU NADH oxidation, which reproduced the equilibrium populations of reduced cofactors observed in EPR spectra. Overall, the results are interpreted in terms of how HoxEFU functions to coordinate electron transfer in reactions with NADH and ferredoxin.

title: Engineering conditional peptide self-assembly using AlphaFold
abstract: Programming self-assembly from peptide sequence remains difficult because existing design rules are only weakly predictive of emergent supramolecular behavior. Here, we show that AlphaFold Multimer can be used to engineer conditional peptide self-assembly by simultaneously selecting for co-assembly and against assembly of the individual components. Using model confidence metrics as proxies for assembly propensity, we designed peptide pairs that largely remain unstructured in isolation but form defined tape-like nanostructures upon mixing. Experimental measurements including circular dichroism, small-angle X-ray scattering, and cryo-electron microscopy validate the predicted behavior across multiple systems. These results establish artificial intelligence-guided design as a practical route to programmable supramolecular peptide materials.

title: Predicting the future of battery lifetime and knee point ultra-early at the formation stage
abstract: Early lifetime prediction can accelerate lithium-ion battery development, support factory-side quality control, and reduce testing-related energy consumption. However, most existing methods rely on post-production cycling data and long test windows, limiting manufacturing scalability. Here, we report an uncertainty-aware framework that jointly predicts battery end of life and the cycle to the knee point directly from formation-stage data. The framework combines physics-informed semantic encoding, a multi-scale convolutional neural network, and temporal attention to extract electrochemically meaningful features, while Monte Carlo Dropout quantifies predictive uncertainty. It achieves a mean absolute error of 46.57 cycles and a mean absolute percentage error of 6.39% for end of life, and 60.80 cycles and 8.57%, respectively, for knee-point prediction. By moving prognostics to the formation stage, this approach reduces dependence on additional cycling tests and enables faster manufacturing feedback for cell screening and formation-protocol evaluation.

title: Physics-informed coarse-mesh framework predicts oxidation-corrosion-deposition in lead-bismuth eutectic systems
abstract: Safety assessment of lead-bismuth eutectic (LBE) energy systems requires predicting coupled oxidation, corrosion, and corrosion product deposition across engineering length and time scales. Existing methods rarely combine sufficient accuracy with practical computational cost, and they often neglect feedback from deposited corrosion products. Here, we report a physics-informed coarse-mesh multiphysics framework for oxidation, corrosion, and deposition analysis in LBE systems. The framework couples corrosion product transport and deposition with oxidation, corrosion, and heat transfer. Comparisons with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and experiments show that it captures key thermohydraulic, mass transfer, oxidation, corrosion, and deposition behavior while reducing central processing unit (CPU) cost by about three orders of magnitude. Full-core simulations of 108 assemblies show that iron-based deposits reduce corrosion removal but increase thermal resistance, while spacer grids either suppress or enhance deposition depending on the dominant mechanism. This framework enables the practical assessment of material degradation and thermal margins in LBE systems.

title: From prediction to understanding: Can artificial intelligence truly learn?
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning (ML) methods are transforming research across the physical sciences. Algorithms capable of truly learning physico-chemical principles could accelerate hypothesis generation and data interpretation and potentially even yield truly novel scientific insights. In this Voices piece, a panel of five experts shares their views on whether current AI/ML methods can truly learn such principles and whether it matters.

title: Why machine learning struggles with magnetism? The role of temperature, disorder, and spin physics
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has transformed materials informatics by enabling rapid prediction, screening, and discovery across vast chemical spaces. However, its application to magnetic materials remains fundamentally constrained. Magnetism presents a particularly stringent representation problem because spin degrees of freedom are coupled to temperature, exchange interactions, spin-orbit coupling, electron correlation, disorder, and microstructure across multiple scales. In contrast, most current ML frameworks rely on static structural or compositional representations, often derived from zero-temperature electronic-structure calculations and ordered materials databases. This mismatch limits their ability to capture the physical mechanisms governing magnetic behavior and frequently reduces prediction to interpolation within restricted datasets. Here, we examine these limitations across major magnetic material classes, including soft magnets, permanent magnets, magnetocaloric materials, two-dimensional magnets, altermagnets, and chemically disordered magnetic systems. We further discuss emerging directions toward physics-informed ML frameworks capable of incorporating thermodynamic evolution, spin interactions, disorder, symmetry, and multiscale magnetic phenomena explicitly.

title: Rhomboid tiling-based topological deep learning for protein complex structure quality assessment beyond pairwise contacts
abstract: Protein complex structure quality assessment remains challenging, particularly with the rapid advancement of generative models such as AlphaFold3, which can produce plausible yet inaccurate structures. Here, we report rhomboid tiling-based topological deep learning (RT-TDL) for protein complex structure quality assessment. RT-TDL represents protein complexes using a hierarchy of order- k Delaunay graphs that capture order- k interactions and organizes them within the rhomboid tiling framework, enabling information propagation within and across different orders. By explicitly modeling higher-order interactions, RT-TDL also highlights biologically meaningful residue combinations. RT-TDL achieves state-of-the-art performance on major protein complex quality assessment benchmarks and ranks as the top-performing single-model method on the CASP EMA dataset, improving correlation by up to 11.9% over existing approaches. RT-TDL further achieves slightly higher AUC scores than AlphaFold3's self-assessment module, highlighting the potential of higher-order structural representations for protein complex modeling.

title: Toward automated discovery with generative models multimodal learning and closed loop workflows in inverse materials design
abstract: Inverse materials design is shifting materials discovery from forward prediction to targeted proposal of candidates that satisfy objectives under physical constraints. Here, we review advances in generative crystal structure modeling, multimodal learning, and closed-loop design pipelines for crystalline solids. We compare generative model classes, including variational autoencoders, normalizing flows, and autoregressive and diffusion models, focusing on their inverse design trade-offs, how physical and chemical constraints are imposed, and how reliably generated candidates survive downstream validation. We examine multimodal learning as a design interface connecting structures with properties, characterization, processing context, and scientific text and coupling these representations with latent optimization, Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, and active learning to guide search under limited validation budgets. We set out recurring failure modes, including surrogate exploitation, diversity collapse, distribution shift, and the stability-synthesizability gap and define a nine-rung discovery-credibility ladder, proposing a minimum reporting standard specifying evidence required to support credible materials discovery claims.

title: Enhancing interpretability of cryo-EM maps using hybrid attention Transformers
abstract: ABSTRACT Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has become a central technique for determining the structures of macromolecular complexes. However, experimental cryo-EM density maps often exhibit limited interpretability due to noise and heterogeneous, anisotropic resolution, complicating downstream atomic model construction. Here we present DEMO-EMReF, a Swin Transformer-based framework specifically designed for cryo-EM density map refinement that integrates channel attention with hybrid spatial attention. By combining local window-based attention with grid-based sparse global attention, DEMO-EMReF captures fine-grained local density features while modeling long-range, cross-region spatial dependencies, enabling more robust density refinement in heterogeneous and anisotropic map regions. DEMO-EMReF was systematically evaluated on large benchmark sets of both primary maps and half-maps spanning resolutions of 3.0-8.0 Å and was compared against multiple state-of-the-art map enhancement methods. DEMO-EMReF consistently improves resolution-related metrics, map-model correlations, and local atomic resolvability, with particularly robust gains in challenging heterogeneous or anisotropic cases. Importantly, the refined maps facilitate more accurate and efficient automated atomic model building. Together, DEMO-EMReF provides a robust approach for enhancing cryo-EM density maps and enabling more reliable downstream studies.

title: Moving beyond thermal conductivity to interfacial networks for next-generation coolants
abstract: Cooling technologies are entering a critical era driven by electrification, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and renewable energy systems. Conventional coolant design remains rooted in a property-centric framework that independently optimizes thermal conductivity, heat capacity, and viscosity. Emerging evidence, including our own studies of nanoparticle-enhanced fluids, reveals non-Einstein behavior in which heat-transfer performance improves while viscosity decreases, challenging the classical suspension theory. We argue that the next frontier lies in understanding, visualizing, and engineering interfacial networks through which the coolant performance should instead be understood. Such networks include the structures and connections formed from the interactions of molecules, particles, and fluidic layers, which collectively govern coupled heat and momentum transport. Progress will require new operando characterization techniques, quantitative network descriptors, and multiscale modeling, ultimately enabling rational design of coolants with unprecedented thermal performance and energy efficiency. This perspective discusses how this framework could guide the design of next-generation coolants.

title: Developing stacking models for interacting biopolymers using quantum mechanical calculations and machine learning
abstract: Biopolymers are long-chain molecules with significant potential for developing sustainable, renewable, and environmentally friendly materials. Agarose, a biopolymer derived from red algae, is widely used in bioengineering and biomedical applications because of its biocompatibility and biodegradability. Understanding how agarose chains interact and assemble is essential for explaining its gelation behavior and material properties. For decades, scientists have debated whether agarose chains primarily form double-helical structures or other arrangements. In this study, researchers used high-throughput quantum mechanical calculations and machine-learning models to investigate the interactions between agarose chains. Their results show that stacked configurations are energetically and statistically more favorable than the traditionally proposed double-helix structure. The study also identifies simple interatomic interactions and distances between specific atomic species as effective descriptors for predicting the assembled structures. These findings resolve a long-standing controversy and provide valuable insight into agarose structure, gelation, and the design of advanced biopolymeric materials.

title: A lean statistical cell-to-pack framework for sustainable battery pack capacity estimation
abstract: Accurate battery pack capacity estimation is vital for electric vehicle and energy storage safety, but conventional pack-level aging tests are costly, energy intensive, and wasteful. This study proposes a lean statistical cell-to-pack (LS-CTP) framework that eliminates pack-level tests. Using aging data from only a few independent test cells, it combines lightweight machine learning and decision algorithms to achieve multi-feature statistical transformation and fusion from routine fragmented charge data. It requires few hyperparameters and low computational overhead and applies to parallel, series, and mixed configurations. Monte Carlo analyses show a mean absolute percentage error below 1.24% for parallel packs and 1.92% for series packs using as few as two test cells. A sustainability assessment indicates over 90% reduction in battery waste and testing energy. By decoupling algorithm development from pack-level cycling, LS-CTP advances cost-effective, energy-efficient, and sustainable battery health diagnostics, supporting the clean energy transition.

title: Emerging and transformative applications of tissue clearing technology in neuroscience research
abstract: Refractive index (RI)-matching-based tissue clearing techniques render intact biological tissues optically transparent, enabling 3D in situ interrogation of nervous systems from whole-brain to single-cell scales. We systematically evaluate three mainstream clearing strategies (hydrophobic, hydrophilic, and hydrogel-based) and summarize their promising applications in neural circuit tracing, tumor research, stem cell therapy, and artificial intelligence (AI) integration. Here, we report that this technology has evolved from a niche imaging tool to an integrated multimodal biotechnological platform. Despite core challenges, including inherent physicochemical trade-offs, optical limits, multi-omics integration biases, and insufficient clinical standardization, future advances in multimodal integration, AI algorithms, and targeted in vivo clearing will drive life science research from static structural mapping toward systematic dissection of dynamic biological processes.

title: Electrochemical memory in LiFePO4 batteries arises from diffusion-driven dynamical asymmetry
abstract: Voltage relaxation in lithium-ion batteries reflects internal electrochemical states but is generally assumed to follow a unique history-independent pathway toward equilibrium. From paired relaxation experiments on LiFePO 4 cells over broad states of health, we show that this assumption is incomplete. Relaxation exhibits "electrochemical memory," a measurable trajectory-level property of nonequilibrium battery relaxation dependent on the charge/discharge history. It shows a robust nonmonotonic dependence on state of charge (SOC), with reduced memory at ∼50%–70% SOC, and an increase toward low and high SOCs. After controlling for SOC, we show that electrochemical memory remains strongly associated with transport-related dynamical asymmetry, supporting a diffusion-mediated interpretation of the observed behavior. Reconstructed phase-space analyses reveal persistent organization of history-dependent relaxation trajectories, while trajectory recoverability demonstrates electrochemical memory encoded throughout relaxation. Overall, voltage relaxation is redefined as an electrochemical-history nonequilibrium dynamical process. Our trajectory-centric framework enables the investigation of electrochemical memory, nonequilibrium battery dynamics, and physics-informed battery diagnostics.

title: A critical audit and methodological roadmap for machine learning in perovskite solar cells
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have advanced from 3.8% to 27.01% power conversion efficiency (PCE) in 17 years, while their lead-free analogs have reached 17.1%, and perovskite/silicon tandems exceeded 34%. Machine learning (ML) is credited with accelerating much of this progress, yet its evaluation is rarely examined. Here, we report a critical audit of 80 ML-PSC studies from 2024 to 2026. Among these, 89% report no error analysis on any sub-range of PCE, none report nested cross-validation, 48% rely on a single train/test split, and only 9% predict stability over time. Models that appear accurate overall can therefore fail in the sparse high-PCE region, which is the region most relevant to commercialization. We reframe high-PCE prediction as an imbalanced regression problem, establish imbalance-aware techniques, recommend an evaluation workflow, and propose a five-pillar roadmap. Further progress depends as much on shared evaluation and reporting standards as on new algorithms.
